title: Quest draft
description: Structured output of the Chancellor (`draftQuests`), passed to Claude Code with --json-schema. One utterance becomes one or more drafts. The Chancellor assigns the tier (script when a catalog script fits, session when judgement is needed), bundles tiny jobs into one quest (usually a batch with units) and splits long work so one quest fits one context (estimate.tokens <= kingdom.breakers.context_budget_tokens), using a plan parent with child drafts. It sets class_required and expertise tags (registry/tags.json). Work that needs several areas (several tags in different parts of a territory) becomes a party: one plan quest with party_role = contract, whose lead (a mage) writes the contract and then emits the parts with this same schema (party_role = part). The Steward adds the merge quest itself. It may ask at most one question. The CLI turns each draft into a create_quest inbox command with draft = true; the Steward writes quests in status draft until the owner confirms.
$comment: Generated by `pnpm schemas` from the zod source in packages/domain/src/schema (ADR 0003): change the zod source, never this file. zod re-validates the CLI's structured_output; for the Gemini tribe (no --json-schema flag) the schema goes into the prompt and the reply is parsed with one retry. Not expressible here, checked by zod: refs unique; depends_on_refs and parent_ref point to other refs in the same output. Not checked by this schema because they need other files: secrets_required within the territory's secrets_allowed (otherwise the draft is dropped); kind, territory and script ids exist.

class_required.description: Required for tier = session; one of kinds[kind].classes_allowed.

party_role.description: contract: the plan quest that forms a party; part: one area of a party, emitted by the party lead. The Steward sets party_id and creates the merge quest.

contract.description: Path of the contract inside the territory; required for a part.

scope_paths.description: The files the quest changes, as globs relative to the territory root (`packages/domain/src/dispatch/**`). Within a territory the Steward never starts a quest whose scope meets the scope a quest holds (from its first run until it is archived, waiting for the owner's merge included), unless its plot is built on that quest's branch; a session-tier quest without a scope runs alone among working quests. Files the work changes outside the scope go into the `quest.submitted` line and the judge's prompt, never an automatic fail. Hot files every branch edits belong in territory.shared_paths, not here.

question.description: The one follow-up question; the quest is created in draft with blocked.question.
